title: Battle Companies rules file
description: Complements a vanilla MESBG definitions file (see vanilla/data2024.schema.json). Units, gear, keywords and magical powers that exist in the vanilla file are referenced by name instead of being redefined.

extends.description: The `game` of the vanilla file this one complements.

names.description: A PRICE GROUP: every name is a distinct item (its own gearAnnotations entry, text and availability) sold at this price. Names are never aliases of each other.

overrides.description: Vanilla keyword this rule replaces: Battle Companies always wins over vanilla.

label.description: Display name when it differs from `name`. `name` is the rule's key (identity: used by specialRules, links, grants); several rules may share a label with different keys (Keen Sight (Falcon) is labelled Keen Sight). The app shows the label, never the key. Absent: the name is both.

relatedTo.description: Other rules (vanilla or Battle Companies keys) this one is a variant of; they share a label and the glossary links them.

table.description: A lookup table the rule prints (a D6 table, a table by combined rating). Rows are ordered; `min`/`max` bound the looked-up number (max null = open ended); `cells` are the printed cells, one per column.

usesRules.description: Rules of the Scenarios chapter this scenario applies, listed under its Special Rules without a text of their own (Maelstrom of Battle, Dark of Night, Heirloom of Power).

outline.description: One-line summary some scenarios carry under the flavour text.

roles.description: Attacker / Defender, for the scenarios that have roles.

scoringObjectives.description: One per Victory Point bullet of `scoring`, in order: what the player is asked and how it scores.

kind.description: tiers: best tier reached or none; each: count x pointsEach; eachTiers: `count` items, each scores its best tier.

reveal.description: secret objectives only: when the player's note is shown to the others.

completion.description: secret objectives only: how the player reports it (the best tier reached, picked at the end).

nomination.description: What the player secretly notes down at the start. from: ownHeroes | enemyHeroes (a Hero model) | terrain (a piece wholly in the opponent's half). Absent: nothing is noted.

allowLeader.description: The Leader may be chosen only when the company has a single Hero.

written.description: The item as the Battle Companies company lists print it.

item.description: The item of the unit's profile the lists are read as; the company lists carry this name.
ownItem only: the data.gearAnnotations item the option is (a weapon of its own, not sold by the Armoury).

armouryItem.description: readAs only: the Armoury item the option is read as.

modifiers.description: Qualities that turn a base item into another one (Elven, Master-forged, Poisoned). An item names its base and its modifiers; the modifier says what it does to the rules, the identity and the price.

glossary.description: The glossary term that defines the rule (shown as the tooltip's link).

identity.description: distinct: the modified item is its own item (a Spear option does not take an Elven spear); variant: it fills the place of its base in a profile option.

appliesTo.description: The kind of weapon the effect matters for.

text.description: The rule, copied from the source.

tooltip.description: The part of `text` shown in an item's tooltip (a prefix of `text`).

price.description: What the Battle Companies document says about the price of such items.

classes.description: What the item IS; the first class is the main one (icon lead, sorting).

grants.description: Special rules the bearer gets: a vanilla keyword, a Battle Companies rule or an instance of a parameterised rule.

aliases.description: Other spellings of the same item (plural, hyphenation).

base.description: The generic item this one is a version of (Elven spear: Spear). Not an alias and not identity: see the modifiers' `identity`.

modifiers.description: Keys of `gearAnnotations.modifiers` that apply to the item; needs `base`.

grantsModifier.description: For a weapon modifier bought for one weapon (Envenom Weapon): the modifier it gives that weapon.

pricedAs.description: Derived from base + the Elven modifier: An Elven-made item sold at the price and rating of its generic equivalent in the wargear table ('Elven-made weaponry uses their generic equivalent values, but are restricted to Elf models'). Its own item, not an alias.

variantOf.description: Derived from base + a `variant` modifier: this item is a specific version of another and fills its place in a profile option (Bow with poisoned arrows is the profile's Bow). Not an alias.

relatedTo.description: Items that are related but DISTINCT (Elf Bow and Longbow share a profile, a Pike is not a Spear). Never an alias: each has its own availability and text. Symmetric.

isA.description: The item's text says 'This is a X': it is X plus extras (Small Shield = Light Shield + Defence against Strikes; Company Horn = War Horn; Elven Glaive = Elven spear + its own rule). It inherits X's classes of use and grants; its own abilities add to X's.

requiresMount.description: Gear only a mounted model can use (a lance, Barding): struck through in a live match when the mount is lost. Absent: usable on foot.

weaponModifier.description: Not an item: a modifier bought for one weapon (Envenom Weapon). The app shows a copy of that weapon with the granted rule.

grantedTo.description: Absent = the bearer gets the rules; `mount` = they belong to the mount (a Pony's Timid).

definition.description: Tooltip text: the source text plus, when the source has none or only a profile, the rulebook text of the item's class.

abilities.description: The same rules as data (support, chargeWoundBonus, defenceBonus, shielding, ...).

profile.description: Where a mount's stat block lives.

id.description: Stable id (bow, throwing, cavalry) that company limitOverrides and limitExemptions refer to.

eligible.description: Who may choose bonuses (the strictly lower rated company, rating compared before the bonuses).

budget.description: The company's rating after the bonuses may not exceed the opponent's (inclusive: equal is allowed).

purchase.description: Tool Kit: one purchase is one Kit, the same Kit never twice.

grants.description: What a bonus gives besides Rating-priced numbers: loaned equipment (Tool Kit), a temporary model (Wanderer), a chosen scenario (Ambush!).

aftermathEffects.description: Every source of re-rolls and aftermath effects: Against the Odds bonuses, scenario rewards and equipment that acts on the injury rolls.

breakPoint.description: When a company is Broken and what follows (Rules Manual Broken Army, Stand Fast; All is Lost!).

persistent.description: Stays on the Hero; counted per Hero (retireAtCount / grantsAtCount work on that count).

healable.description: Can be removed by treatment or by a healOneInjury result.

retireAtCount.description: The Nth occurrence retires the Hero as per the Dead result.

healableBy.description: Treatment methods (campaign.injuries.treatment.hero[].key) that can remove this status when it is not a persistent injury.

maxTotal.description: minorSpecialRule / heroicAction: most the Hero may have in total.

offers.description: What taking the path gives a Hero, derived from the path's own data (for the path picker's tooltip).

summary.description: One short text: the starting Heroic Action / Magical Power, the path's special rules and Mastery, the characteristics level-ups improve, the other choices.

masteryRule.description: The path's Mastery rule (it improves a Heroic Action).

specialRules.description: The path's own special rules in chart order, without the Mastery rule.

signatureStats.description: The characteristics improved together with the Mastery rule (the path's signature characteristic).

items.description: Models taken out of the listed limits (ids of the top-level limits): left out of both the count and the base the maximum is worked out on.

aftermathEffect.description: Key of campaign.aftermathEffects[] this item activates (Healing Herbs, Wondrous Cram).
